hypotheses.title: Incremental 24-hour volatility forecasting
hypotheses.claim: Funding extremes plus price-dislocation/smoothing features improve out-of-sample forecasts of next-24-hour realized variance of mark-price returns over a realized-volatility-only HAR-style baseline.
hypotheses.estimand: Paired out-of-sample QLIKE difference (C2 vs B1) on the frozen test panel.

prior_tests.result: C2 vs B1: -2.50% relative QLIKE reduction; 95% CI [-0.123401, 0.158843] crosses zero; test window single ~4-day block

hypotheses.next_falsification_test: Pre-registered FCLR-002 (or later) with >=3 non-overlapping 30-day evaluation blocks across >=5 instruments, uncertainty supporting improvement after multiplicity correction, before any risk-overlay phase.

hypotheses.title: Funding-extreme correction-time replication
hypotheses.claim: The working-paper pattern (Shek, SSRN, posted 29 Sep 2026) of shorter median funding-extreme correction times in low-volatility versus high-volatility conditions can be independently reconstructed from admissible public Binance data.
hypotheses.estimand: Median/mean time-to-correction among corrected funding-extreme events, split by realized-volatility regime.
hypotheses.directional_claim: Correction time lower in low-volatility conditions.
hypotheses.status_evidence: scripts/funding_correction_replication.py; tests/test_funding_correction_replication.py (4/4 passed); 445 funding-extreme events across 5 symbols Jan-Mar 2024

prior_tests.result: Median correction time 8.0h, mean 12.6h among corrected events (Jan-Mar 2024, 5 symbols)
prior_tests.verdict: Partial: full paper methodology not independently reconstructible from public sources alone

hypotheses.next_falsification_test: Obtain and document the paper's full event-definition and censoring rules; if unavailable, report as partial replication and do not promote correction-time association to volatility-forecast or liquidation evidence.

hypotheses.title: Hypothetical boundary-breach forecast
hypotheses.claim: Funding and price-dislocation features improve out-of-sample forecasts of whether mark prices breach a precomputed hypothetical long/short liquidation boundary within a pre-specified horizon under disclosed margin/leverage assumptions.
hypotheses.estimand: Brier score / log loss / precision-recall on synthetic mark-price boundary-breach labels.
hypotheses.directional_claim: Candidate models beat the volatility-only baseline on breach probability.
hypotheses.status_evidence: No out-of-sample breach evaluation has been run; labels are implemented but unvalidated against holdout.
hypotheses.next_falsification_test: Register margin/leverage scenarios before examining any outcomes; run only under a new pre-registered protocol version with sufficient data.

hypotheses.title: Observed liquidation outcomes
hypotheses.claim: Funding extremes predict observed forced-liquidation events or liquidation-notional intensity.
hypotheses.estimand: Event/liquidation-notional intensity normalized by open interest or volume.
hypotheses.directional_claim: Funding features add predictive value for observed liquidations.
hypotheses.status_evidence: research_state/binance_source_probe.md: no liquidationSnapshot archive found (HTTP 404); Binance fapi forceOrders endpoint returns 451 restricted location in this environment.
hypotheses.next_falsification_test: Enumerate and test additional admissible public liquidation sources (academic/GitHub/Zenodo/Hugging Face archives, other venue-native historical archives) before concluding Track A is unviable; do not infer event-free intervals from missing data.
